1.title: Building Great Agent Skills: The Missing Manual
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Skills need explicit design decisions on trigger (user-invoked vs model-invoked), internal structure, steering mechanism, and pruning — and there's a concrete checklist to evaluate them against.

2.title: Deterministic Infra for Non-Deterministic AI Agents - Nishant Gupta, Meta Superintelligence Labs
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Never let the model directly control production systems — separate proposal generation from validation/approval/execution via a policy engine and execution gateway, turning infrastructure into the reliability layer rather than the model.

3.title: Gusto’s CTO deleted everything and replaced it with Claude Code - here’s what happened
3.author: How I AI
3.hook: A 1000-person R&D org rebuilt a tier-one product (Co-founder) in 10 weeks with 4 engineers + 1 designer using Claude Code + Cloudflare Workers + Vercel AI SDK, shipping with zero meetings, no Jira, no design debt — treating code as disposable and rebuilding from scratch as reasonable.

4.title: The Prompt is the Platform - Dominik Tornow, Resonate HQ
4.author: AI Engineer
4.hook: Agents don't jump from abstract spec to concrete implementation in one step — they need a deterministic simulation layer first to discover correct algorithms under failure, then emit a concrete spec, then production code.

5.title: Why OpenAI is merging Codex and ChatGPT and the future of knowledge work | Andrew Ambrosino
5.author: Lenny's Podcast
5.hook: At OpenAI, the cost inversion is real — implementation via LLMs is now cheap; the expensive part is taste/curation. This flips product process: instead of derisk-through-design-upfront, teams now build 90 uncoordinated explorations and synthesize afterward.

6.title: Your Agent Failed in Prod. Good Luck Reproducing It. - Tisha Chawla & Susheem Koul, Microsoft
6.author: AI Engineer
6.hook: Agent bugs in production aren't reproducible because determinism isn't the constraint—replayability (recording inputs/outputs at system boundaries, not network layer) is; this shifts debugging from "make the model deterministic" to "make the run observable and replayable without model calls."

7.title: Every employee should be a one-person startup
7.author: Peter Yang
7.hook: Individual agent augmentation (one person + agents doing work that previously required cross-team requests) unlocks autonomy and creative output faster than optimizing multi-team processes, and should be the sequencing foundation before tackling org-wide workflows.

8.title: Frontier results, on device - RL Nabors, Arize
8.author: AI Engineer
8.hook: Small language models (SLMs) running on-device can eliminate most inference costs (security, latency, connectivity, token spend) while consuming equal or less energy than frontier models for task-specific work.

9.title: I benchmarked the NEW Sonnet 5. The results shocked me.
9.author: How I AI
9.hook: Building repeatable, human-graded benchmarks for model evaluation using Claude Code and past session history as context—moving from one-off vibe checks to systematic eval design.

10.title: The "Trash Can Method" for software development
10.author: How I AI
10.hook: Cost of code is so low with AI that you can validate product-market fit with a throwaway V1, then rebuild from scratch in a V2 branch rather than iterate on flawed architecture.
